narrative:
Based on your application, our system has determined that you represent a higher-than-acceptable credit risk, leading to the denial of your loan. The model calculated a 58% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning it was more likely than not that you would struggle to repay the loan. This decision was not based on personal factors like your age or sex, but on specific financial indicators from your application.

The most significant factor was the status of your checking account, which showed a negative balance. This is a strong warning sign, as most approved applicants have a positive or at least a zero balance. This single factor pushed the decision strongly toward denial.

The second most important factor was the length of the loan you requested, which was 42 months. This is more than double the average of 19 months for approved applicants. A longer repayment period increases the bank's risk, as more time allows for unforeseen financial difficulties.

Interestingly, your credit history actually worked in your favor. Having a record of "critical/other credits" is common among approved applicants, and this factor slightly nudged the prediction toward approval. However, this positive influence was not enough to overcome the negative impact of your account status and loan duration.

Your application also showed other risk indicators. You are currently unemployed, while most approved applicants have stable employment. You requested a loan for repairs, a purpose that is very rare among approved applicants. Additionally, you have a higher installment rate relative to your income and no telephone, which are both associated with higher risk.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on stabilizing your checking account and building a positive balance. Consider applying for a smaller loan with a shorter repayment period. Securing any form of employment, even part-time, would significantly strengthen your application. Addressing these key areas will demonstrate greater financial stability and reduce the perceived risk to lenders.
